chunks: And with the preceding chains of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Numan al-Ajali, who said: Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, said:

"O Abu al-Numan, do not fabricate lies against us, lest you be stripped of the True Faith (al-Hanifiyyah). O Abu al-Numan, do not exploit people through us, for God will only increase you in poverty thereby. O Abu al-Numan, do not seek leadership, lest you become a tail.
O Abu al-Numan, you will surely be stopped and questioned, and there is no escape from that! If you are truthful, we shall confirm your truthfulness; and if you lie, we shall confirm your falsehood.

O Abu al-Numan, let not people deceive you about yourself, for the matter shall reach you regardless of them. And do not waste your day with this and that, for with you is One who records everything against you. And do good, for I have not seen anything swifter in attainment nor more relentless in pursuit than a good deed overtaking an old sin."

key_terms.الْحَنِيفِيَّةَ: al-Hanifiyyah: the True Monotheistic Faith, the straight path of Abraham
key_terms.دَرَكًا: darak: attainment, reaching; here meaning how quickly a good deed catches up to erase an old sin
key_terms.ذَنَبًا: dhanab: literally 'tail', metaphor for being a follower rather than a leader

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir (AS) advise Abu al-Numan about truthfulness and good deeds?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) delivers a series of five direct exhortations to his companion Abu al-Numan al-Ajali. The Imam warns against fabricating lies about the Ahl al-Bayt, exploiting people in their name, seeking leadership for its own sake, being deceived by others, and wasting time. He concludes with an encouragement that good deeds are the swiftest remedy for past sins. This teaching reflects the Imam's concern about opportunists who used the name of the Imams for personal gain, a recurring problem in early Shia communities.
